ic_name: MIPI SPMI v2.0 + RFFE v3.0 (System Power Management + RF Front-End Control)

clock_and_reset_waveform.POR_release: After Power-On Reset, devices must release both SDA and SCL (drive HIGH-Z) before any transaction.

bit_transfer_waveform.rule: Data on SDA must be stable while SCL is HIGH (data valid window). SDA may change while SCL is LOW (change-of-data window).
bit_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 4 — Bit transfer on the I2C-bus

data_transfer_waveform.byte_unit: 8 data bits + 1 ACK clock = 9 SCL pulses per byte
data_transfer_waveform.ack_position: On the 9th SCL pulse; receiver pulls SDA LOW
data_transfer_waveform.figure: Figure 6 — Data transfer on the I2C-bus

arbitration_waveform.spmi: Masters contend on SDATA during the arbitration window before the SSC; higher priority / lower MASTER_ID wins; a slave Request is asserted in the same window.

bus_waveform.ssc: Sequence Start Condition — SDATA pulse while SCLK is low — starts a transaction.
bus_waveform.bit_sampling: MSB-first; SDATA sampled on the defined SCLK edge.
bus_waveform.parity: one odd parity bit follows each command/address/data frame.
bus_waveform.bus_park: Bus Park Cycle (SCLK toggling, SDATA released) ends the transaction.

transaction_waveform.generic: SSC | Command Frame + parity | [Address Frame + parity] | [Data Frame + parity ...] | Bus Park Cycle
transaction_waveform.register_0_write: SSC | Command Frame (incl. 7 data bits) + parity | Bus Park Cycle
transaction_waveform.extended: ...Command | Address | byte count | Data1..DataN + parity each | Bus Park

trigger_waveform.rffe: Trigger-register values are pre-loaded; a Trigger event applies them to several slaves simultaneously.

clock_waveform.source: master-supplied SCLK; no clock recovery; no forwarded-clock lane.

general_timing_rule: SPMI/RFFE are synchronous to the master-supplied SCLK. Each frame is MSB-first plus one odd parity bit. An SSC starts a transaction and a Bus Park Cycle ends it. SPMI resolves multi-master arbitration before the SSC; RFFE has a single master. RFFE triggers apply pre-loaded values simultaneously across slaves.
